claim: TuRBO's trust region is an explicit hyperrectangle centered at the best solution found so far, whose side length is adapted by a hand-designed deterministic success/failure counter (doubled after tau_succ consecutive improvements, halved after tau_fail consecutive non-improvements), not a region that emerges implicitly from an acquisition function.
stance_target: N4: the implicit-trust-region-via-LCB framing (growing GP variance under LCB creates an emergent trust region) is owned by TuRBO
scope_conditions: TuRBO trust-region-BO algorithm, high-dimensional black-box optimization
quoted_support: We choose our TR to be a hyperrectangle centered at the best solution found so far... After tau_succ consecutive successes, we double the size of the TR, i.e., L <- min{L_max, 2L}. After tau_fail consecutive failures, we halve the size of the TR: L <- L/2.

claim: TuRBO uses Thompson Sampling, not LCB, to select candidates within each trust region; 'LCB' / 'lower confidence bound' does not appear anywhere in the paper.
stance_target: N4: LCB + growing GP variance = implicit trust region is owned by TuRBO
scope_conditions: Full-text grep of extracted PDF, ~9,290 words
quoted_support: we find that TS provides a principled solution to both the problem of selecting candidates within a single TR, and selecting candidates across the set of trust regions simultaneously.

claim: TuRBO's own diagnosis treats unchecked global GP posterior-variance growth as a PROBLEM under myopic acquisition functions -- it causes overemphasized exploration and failure to exploit promising areas -- rather than as a mechanism that automatically confers a beneficial implicit trust region.
stance_target: N4: growing GP variance alone (without an externally imposed geometric constraint) is sufficient to create a helpful implicit trust region
scope_conditions: High-dimensional BO with myopic (non-batch, non-trust-region) acquisition functions
quoted_support: the fact that search spaces grow considerably faster than sampling budgets due to the curse of dimensionality implies the inherent presence of regions with large posterior uncertainty. For common myopic acquisition functions, this results in an overemphasized exploration and a failure to exploit promising areas.

claim: Candidates in TuRBO are explicitly restricted to lie within the pre-defined trust region hyperrectangle at each iteration; if the TR were expanded to cover the whole space, TuRBO would reduce to standard global BO.
stance_target: N4: mechanics of TuRBO's trust region, for distinguishing explicit vs. implicit framing
quoted_support: we utilize an acquisition function at each iteration t to select a batch of q candidates... restricted to be within the TR. If L was large enough for the TR to contain the whole space, this would be equivalent to running standard global BO.
